title: Linking words
intro: Linking words connect your ideas. Start with the basic ones, then use more advanced words to show contrast and comparison in speaking and writing.

sources.label: British Council: Using as and like

sections.title: Linking words: and, but, because, so
sections.summary: Use simple linking words to join ideas.

tables.caption: Basic linking words
head: word
function
example
rows: I like tea but not coffee.
I stayed at home because I was ill.
I was ill, so I stayed at home.
Do you want tea or coffee?
We had lunch, then we went for a walk.

uses: Because answers why, so gives the result. Do not use both: Because I was ill, so I stayed at home is wrong.
Put a comma before so and but when they join two clauses with different subjects.
Because can start the sentence: Because it was raining, we stayed in.
Because of is followed by a noun: because of the rain.

examples.text: I went to bed early because I was tired.
It was cold, so we stayed inside.
We stayed in because of the rain.

mistakes.wrong: Because I was tired, so I went to bed.
mistakes.right: Because I was tired, I went to bed.

mistakes.wrong: We stayed home because the rain.
mistakes.right: We stayed home because of the rain.

checks.question: Choose: It was late, (because / so) we took a taxi.
Choose: I stayed home (because / so) I was ill.

sections.title: Contrasting ideas: although, despite and others
sections.summary: Use these words to show that two ideas are different or surprising together.

tables.caption: Contrast words
head: word
followed by
example
rows: Although it was cold, we went swimming.
Despite the cold, we went swimming.
clause (at the start of the second clause)
It was cold, but we went swimming.
It was cold. However, we went swimming.
Tom likes sport, while his brother likes art.

uses: Although and but cannot be used together in the same sentence: Although it was cold, we went. (not Although ... but ...).
Despite and in spite of take a noun or an -ing form. Do not add of after despite.
Despite the fact that + clause is possible.
However is stronger than but and is used in writing. Put a full stop or a semicolon before it.

examples.text: Despite feeling ill, she went to work.
She was tired. However, she kept working.
He is rich, whereas his brother is poor.
examples.note: Whereas shows a contrast between two people or things.

mistakes.wrong: Despite of the rain, we went out.
mistakes.right: Despite the rain, we went out.
mistakes.why: Despite has no of. In spite of has of.

mistakes.wrong: Although it was cold, but we went out.
mistakes.right: Although it was cold, we went out.
mistakes.why: Do not use but with although.

mistakes.wrong: In spite he was ill, he went.
mistakes.right: In spite of being ill, he went.
mistakes.why: Use in spite of with a noun or -ing.

checks.question: Rewrite with despite: Although it rained, we played.
Choose: (Although / Despite) she was tired, she studied.

sections.title: Using as and like
sections.summary: As and like are different. Use like to compare and as to say a role or a job.

tables.caption: As and like
head: word
use
example
rows: He is as tall as me.
It looks as if it will rain.
I like fruit such as apples.

uses: Like + noun / pronoun: He runs like the wind.
As + noun for a job or a function: She used a book as a pillow.
As + clause for the way something is done: Do it as I showed you.
As if + clause for a possibility: He talks as if he knew everything.

examples.text: She works as a guide in a museum.
It sounds as if you are happy.

mistakes.wrong: She is as like her mother.
mistakes.why: Do not combine as and like.

checks.question: Complete: I use my phone ___ an alarm clock.
Complete: He looks ___ his father.
checks.explanation: A comparison with a noun: like.
